name: Microsoft 365 Personal
tagline: Sync selected files and provide a personal document library on user-owned storage

pricing.notes: Official monthly Personal subscription in the US.

tiers.name: Microsoft account / Outlook
tiers.limits: 5 GB OneDrive storage and 15 GB Outlook mailbox storage; web and mobile Office apps.

tiers.name: Microsoft 365 Basic
tiers.limits: 100 GB OneDrive storage and 100 GB Outlook mailbox storage for 1 person.

tiers.name: Microsoft 365 Personal
tiers.limits: 1 TB storage for 1 person; sign in on 5 devices simultaneously; desktop Office apps with Copilot.

tiers.name: Microsoft 365 Family
tiers.limits: 1-6 people; 1 TB per person, up to 6 TB total; 5 simultaneous devices per person.
tiers.notes: $129.99 billed yearly; AI benefits are primarily for the subscription owner; 1-month trial.

tiers.name: Microsoft 365 Premium
tiers.limits: 1-6 people and up to 6 TB total; highest personal Copilot usage and advanced agent features.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 5 GB OneDrive storage and 15 GB Outlook mailbox storage
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (up to about 17% lower yearly); subscriptions auto-renew until cancelled
pricing.hiddenCosts: Personal and Family storage can be expanded up to 10 TB through extra OneDrive storage, but the current add-on prices were not exposed. Family AI entitlements are not shared equally: key Copilot benefits are limited to the subscription owner.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Microsoft 365 Personal, sync selected files and provide a personal document library on user-owned storage. The hard boundary is office applications, onedrive sync, device support, identity, and global infrastructure, plus reliability, durability, and cross-device sync.
coreLoopDIY: Sync selected files into a personal document library on user-owned storage, encrypt them client-side, track versions, and restore from user-owned object storage.
whatYouLose: Office applications, OneDrive sync, device support, identity, and global infrastructure
ongoingBurden: chunking, encryption, conflict detection, versions, garbage collection, bandwidth, restore drills, monitoring, billing, and disaster recovery
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Microsoft 365 Personal because storage subscriptions sell confidence that files will still exist after a lost device, bad sync, or provider incident. The recurring cost buys chunking, encryption, conflict detection, versions, garbage collection, bandwidth, restore drills, monitoring, billing, and disaster recovery, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Nextcloud
priorArt.desc: Mature open-source file sync and collaboration server.

alternatives.name: Nextcloud Files
alternatives.desc: A personal file library with sync, versions, and sharing; Word and Excel are not hiding in the container.

facts.install: Deploy Nextcloud All-in-One with Docker, or perform a manual web-server, PHP and database installation
facts.dataFormat: Files live in the configured local data directory or object storage; metadata, shares, versions and application state live in a supported SQL database
facts.gapVsPaid: It supplies storage and sharing but does not include Word, Excel, PowerPoint or Microsoft's browser coauthoring experience.
facts.setupBlocker: A server plus Docker or a full web stack, DNS and TLS, and a plan for upgrades, backups and storage failures

alternatives.name: OpenCloud
alternatives.desc: A user-owned document library with desktop and mobile sync, minus Microsoft’s office-suite gravity.

facts.install: Use the documented Docker Compose and Traefik stack; a single-binary deployment is also possible
facts.dataFormat: The base deployment stores file data and metadata in its configured POSIX instance directory; an optional decomposed backend stores blobs in S3 and metadata on POSIX storage
facts.gapVsPaid: It is a document library, not an office suite; browser editing requires a separate WOPI-compatible editor.
facts.setupBlocker: Docker, a domain and open ports, reverse-proxy and TLS configuration, and operational responsibility for the storage directory

alternatives.name: Seafile Community Edition
alternatives.desc: A fast personal document library with versioning; browser Office editing needs another product.

facts.install: Deploy the Community Edition with the official Docker Compose stack
facts.dataFormat: File libraries are stored as deduplicated blocks with Git-like repository, commit and filesystem objects rather than ordinary folders, while metadata lives in relational databases
facts.gapVsPaid: It does not include Office applications or native coauthoring, and its block store is not a plain server-side document folder.
facts.setupBlocker: Docker Compose, MariaDB, Caddy or another proxy, a domain and TLS, plus coordinated backups of both databases and block storage

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Personal plan and a single-user encrypted backup DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Microsoft 365 Personal in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, MinIO, and a Tauri 2 sync client; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: sync selected files into a personal document library on user-owned storage, encrypt them client-side, track versions, and restore from user-owned object storage.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Build a desktop client that watches explicitly selected folders and ignores configured patterns.
Chunk, hash, compress, and encrypt files locally before uploading to the configured object store.
Store version metadata, tombstones, device identifiers, and integrity checks in PostgreSQL.
Provide upload and restore queues with pause, retry, bandwidth limits, and resumable transfers.
Add file history, point-in-time restore, key export, storage usage, and scheduled restore tests.
Document the failure model and make clear that one server is not a complete backup strategy.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out multi-provider consumer sync at global scale.
Deliberately leave out guaranteed durability or ransomware recovery.
Deliberately leave out shared-drive administration, mobile apps, and enterprise compliance.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
